A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HeadKV research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, retrieval and reasoning tests, and memory/latency measurements in Sections 4.2–4.5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds beta sensitivity and validation/test analyses in Figures 10–11.

M1.justification: Both versions use retrieval-reasoning head scores, proportional allocation from a shared cache budget, and SnapKV selection within heads. The normalization statement and new pseudocode document the existing procedure rather than establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same LongBench and LooGLE tasks and needle/reasoning-in-a-haystack scenarios. The additional LongBench summarization, few-shot, synthetic, and code results already appear in v1 Appendix C. The new validation split retains existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: FullKV, SnapKV, PyramidKV, Ada-SnapKV, and the relevant HeadKV variants. Table 6 retains its narrower comparator set. Newly discussed context-compression methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v4 Figure 11 introduces a supplementary protocol using 15% of each of six LongBench datasets for validation and the remainder for testing, selecting beta on validation for Llama-3-8B-Instruct at cache sizes 128 and 1024. This does not establish that the unchanged main tables were recomputed under that protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds focused analyses of sensitivity to the shared-budget parameter beta and validation-based beta selection, shown in Figures 10–11. The existing component ablation, head visualizations, and detailed haystack analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that peak-memory results average three trials. v4 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Its validation/test split concerns evaluation design rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged, including the Llama-3-8B-Instruct HeadKV-R2 LongBench average of 32.00 at cache size 128. v4 newly reports beta-dependent scores and validation/test curves in Figures 10–11. These are supplementary results, not improved scores under the original settings.

T1.justification: v4 explicitly specifies the unit-sum normalization of allocation weights in Section 3.2 and states the upper bound of one for Equation 2 scores in Appendix E. These modestly extend the mathematical specification. Added decoding-step indices are notation clarifications; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims: head-level allocation guided by retrieval-reasoning importance, strong compression performance, and retaining 97% of full-cache performance with 1.5% of the cache.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of distractors and correct-answer scoring, interprets beta sensitivity, and identifies possible multi-GPU synchronization overhead in Appendix I. Its new stability interpretation is overstated: Appendix G claims both variants outperform Ada-SnapKV across tested betas, while Figure 10 shows Llama HeadKV-R below it at several settings.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands reproducibility information: two calibration templates, five haystack lengths and ten depths yielding 100 examples per model, normalization and allocation pseudocode, one-time budget initialization, and selected beta values in Table 4. It clarifies selection by average performance and supplies code/data access information where v1 only promised future code availability.

R1.justification: v4 adds Ge et al. (2024a) and an Appendix H discussion positioning KV-cache compression against LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, ICAE, and DODO. This extends discussion to neighboring prompt and representation compression approaches while retaining the original positioning against layer-constrained cache allocation.

P1.justification: The main narrative and Sections 1–5 remain largely verbatim. Changes comprise localized wording and notation explanations, the publication header, and added appendix sections E–I for construction details, pseudocode, hyperparameters, discussion, and limitations.

P2.justification: The appendix display material expands substantially through new Figures 9–11, pseudocode Listing 1, and a reformatted Table 4 with a beta column. Existing appendix figures are repositioned; v1 Figures 9–10 survive as v4 Figures 12–13. Main figures receive only small label and caption corrections.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility through calibration details, selected hyperparameters, pseudocode, and access information. The validation analysis and explicit multi-GPU limitation also improve assessability. These gains are tempered by unchanged best-of-grid main reporting and Appendix G's robustness claim contradicting Figure 10. The net improvement is limited but supported, principally in transparency and supporting analysis.
